name: requests_filter
description: Reports the outcome of analyzing the user's request: whether it is an actionable Infrastructure as Code (IaC) change with Terraform in the current workspace, the answer to an informational question about the workspace infrastructure (inventory, possible improvements, change impact), or a rejection. This tool must be called as the final action, after inspecting the workspace, before attempting to construct any infrastructure information or proceeding with IaC generation.

status.description: True ONLY if the user's request is a change request: creating, modifying, or deleting cloud infrastructure with Terraform, executable in this workspace. Missing parameters never make it False: naming conventions, resource module templates, and workspace state supply the defaults. False for everything else: informational questions about the workspace infrastructure (answered in `explanation`), requests outside the scope of IaC, requests violating a prohibited action, requests targeting an existing resource that cannot be unambiguously identified from the request, workspace, or history, or requests referencing as existing something not present in the workspace.

explanation.description: When status is true (change request): a concise enumeration of the defaults and assumptions being applied (e.g., which existing resource group, name per naming conventions, remaining settings from the module template) — this is passed to the downstream generation chains. When status is false, this text is shown to the user verbatim: for informational questions it MUST contain the complete, self-contained answer based on the workspace evidence; for rejections it states exactly what is out of scope, prohibited, ambiguous, or missing from the workspace.
